goal: `mc test <repo> <pr>` is the one verb that answers "is this change red?", and it answers it fast. When it knows the repository it reads that repository's instruction — what to select, how to run it, what to run beside the tests — instead of mc carrying hardcoded knowledge about each repository in its own source.

Two things are wrong today and this project fixes both. The round is not complete: memoro's selector reports `commands` beside `files` — `css:lint`, `css:tokens`, `i18n:contract`, `i18n:locale-contract`, `i18n:validate`, `sql:pr-ci`, `sdk:check` — and `selectFiles` in `src/mc/repo-gate.js` reads `files` and drops the rest, so a round measures the tests and none of the contract gates. And the round is slow for reasons nobody has measured: it runs the same file list on both sides when ruling 4 says the candidate alone, it schedules alphabetically when four files of twenty carry three quarters of the wall time, and it runs in a fresh worktree every round without anyone knowing what that costs.
When this is done, a round runs what the repository says to run, once, on the candidate, ordered so the expensive files start first, and it says how long each part took and how far it reached.
contract: `mc test` never merges anything. `repo-gate.js` asserts against its own source that no merge call exists in it — *"There is no way to merge a red gate. Not a flag, not an option, not an environment variable."* That assertion stays, and `mc merge` keeps paying for the measurement `mc test` performs rather than growing a second one.

The instruction is data about a repository, not logic inside mc. mc may ship a fallback entry, but this project adds no new hardcoded knowledge about a named repository to mc's source — it moves what is there behind a declaration the repository itself can carry.

The verdict stays differential and carries its own reach: how many files the selection chose, what the selection is blind to, and — once step 4 lands — at which commit the comparison set was measured and how long ago. A round never reports "everything is green".
No test is deleted, skipped, or reclassified to make a round faster. Speed comes from ordering, concurrency, and not running the same work twice.
out_of_scope: `mc merge`'s landing sequence. It calls `runGate` and lands what came back clean; nothing about the merge half changes here.

The worktree form of the verb — `mc test` against a working tree with no pull request, for sessions analysing the repository rather than a change. Ruling 4 settled that the PR form comes first and the worktree form is its own step afterwards, not a condition for it.
Deleting or consolidating tests. That is `test-architecture`'s `test-value-cleanup` in memoro, and this project's contract forbids touching test membership.

Completing memoro's own `npm run ci` — the deterministic checks that today live only in `workflow_dispatch:`-only workflows and therefore run nowhere: `check:validators` (2.0 s), `check:bsqlite-pin` (2.6 s, red on main today), `legal:gate` (2.3 s), `holidays:check` (1.1 s), `corpus:cards:check` (1.5 s), and the three bash guards in `pr-quality-gate.yml` (raw `console.*` in `src/`, static `logger.<level>` with `userId`, migration number collisions). Those belong in memoro's registry as command bindings, which is a memoro project. This project makes sure that whatever `npm run ci` selects actually runs in a round; it does not decide what `npm run ci` should select.

`vendor:check` as a gate. It is red right now because mermaid and pptxgenjs have newer upstream versions — red for every diff, including the empty one. It is a drift notice, not a change gate, and nothing here should treat it as one.

success_criteria.criterion: A round runs the command gates the repository's selection reported, not only its test files.
success_criteria.check: `mc test memoro <pr>` on a pull request touching only `public/css/` shows `css:lint` and `css:tokens` in the verdict with their own timings; a pull request that breaks `i18n:contract` comes back red naming that command. Both run against a real PR, not a fixture.

success_criteria.criterion: What to run for a repository is read from a declaration, and mc's shipped table is only the fallback.
success_criteria.check: `declarationFor` returns the repository's own `.mc/test.json` fields over the shipped entry and under `~/mc/repo-gates.json`; `tests/mc/repo-gate-table.test.js` covers all three precedence levels, and a repository with no file behaves exactly as it does today.

success_criteria.criterion: The candidate side is measured alone, against a recorded set, and the report says how old that set is.
success_criteria.check: A round's JSON report carries no baseline suite run, names the commit the comparison set was measured at and how many commits ago, and warns loudly — without refusing — when that is stale. Ruling 4, condition 3.

success_criteria.criterion: The round knows what its own files cost and starts the expensive ones first.
success_criteria.check: After two rounds a cost table under `~/mc/` names per-file wall times for the repository; the third round's file order is descending by recorded cost, asserted in a unit test against a synthetic table.

success_criteria.criterion: The suite phase of a round is measurably faster than the baseline this plan recorded, on the same list.
success_criteria.check: The 20 `tests/surface-runtime/*.test.js` files named in the lessons below run in a median of at most 6.0 s over five runs on this machine, against the 11.1 / 12.4 / 9.3 s recorded here at concurrency 2. Five runs because the spread on this measurement is about 30 %.

what_the_code_taught_us.title: The round reads `files` and throws away `commands`
body: `selectFiles` in `src/mc/repo-gate.js` (main, around line 875) parses the selector's JSON and takes `parsed?.files`. Nothing reads `commands`, and `extra_gates` for memoro in `src/mc/repo-gate-table.js` is `Object.freeze([])`.

Measured 2026-08-30 in the memoro worktree: `node scripts/testing/ci.mjs --list --json --changed-path public/css/molecules/hero-card.css` reports 18 test files **and** two commands, `css:lint` and `css:tokens`. A round over that change runs the 18 files and neither command. The same holds for `i18n:contract`, `i18n:locale-contract`, `i18n:validate`, `sql:pr-ci` and `sdk:check`, which memoro's registry declares as `ciBindings[].commands`.

This is a regression introduced with `select`. Before `select` was declared, the round ran `npm test` — which is `scripts/testing/ci.mjs`, which runs its own selected commands. Swapping the whole gate for a file list dropped every contract gate the gate had.

what_the_code_taught_us.title: `affected` is declared, normalised nowhere, and read by dead code
body: `src/mc/repo-freshen.js:9` describes the freshen step as "run its declared `affected`". `normalise()` in `src/mc/repo-gate-table.js` on main returns `prepare`, `prepare_why`, `select`, `select_why`, `extra_gates`, `merge_log`, `pr_tests_flags` — and no `affected`. So `declaration.affected` is `undefined` for every repository and that path never runs.

Ruling 4 declared memoro's `affected` as `npm run ci -- --base-ref origin/main` and memoro-cli's as `ownTests`. Neither is reachable. The field is one line in `normalise`, and it is the line that makes the ruling's A measurement possible at all.

what_the_code_taught_us.title: The wall time is four files, and the numbers are noisy
body: Twenty files from `tests/surface-runtime/`, timed on this machine (8 cores, 8 GiB, Node v24.10.0) with `--test-reporter=tap` and `--import ./tests/_helpers/browser-paths.mjs`: concurrency 2 gave 11.1, 12.4 and 9.3 s across three runs; concurrency 4 gave 8.1 s; concurrency 8 gave 8.9 s; no flag at all (Node's default, `availableParallelism() - 1` = 7) gave 9.9 s.

Timed one at a time, four of the twenty carry the load: `anchored-surface-contract.test.js` 6.19 s, `account-command-runtime.test.js` 4.05, `app-query-runtime.test.js` 3.87, `admin-command-runtime.test.js` 3.41 — about 17.5 s of roughly 23 s serial. Warm, the heaviest file alone is 4.33 s, which is the floor no amount of concurrency gets under. Twenty files from `tests/ui/` were 101 tests in 3.0 s serially, about 0.15 s a file: ten times cheaper. So "a test costs two seconds" is true of `surface-runtime` and false of the rest, and an average over the tree hides both facts.

More workers buys 11 s → 8 s, roughly 1.37×. Ordering should buy more: with a 4.3 s floor and about 23 s of work over 8 lanes, longest-first has a makespan near 5 s where alphabetical order has 8–11. Neither has been tried. The spread between identical runs was about 30 %, so any claim about a change here needs a median of at least three runs, and preferably five.

One first-run measurement came out at 31.4 s for the same twenty files, against 9–12 s on every later run. That was not isolated — the reporter differed and the machine was doing other work — so it is recorded as unexplained rather than as a cold-start cost. It matters because `runGate` builds a **fresh worktree** for every round, so if there is a cold cost, every round pays it twice. Step 5 measures it rather than assuming it.

what_the_code_taught_us.title: Two caps, and only one of them binds a round
body: memoro's own runner caps itself hard: `RESOURCE_CAPACITY = 2` in `scripts/testing/resource-coordinator.mjs:15`, and `RESOURCE_BATCHES` in `scripts/testing/runner.mjs:10` declares `standard: 2, sqlite: 1, heavy: 1`. That is a constant `2` on an eight-core machine, and it binds every local `npm run ci`.

It does **not** bind a `mc test` round today, because `measureSelected` spawns `node --test --test-reporter=tap ...files` directly (`repo-gate.js` around line 1157) with no `--test-concurrency` at all, so those runs take Node's default of seven. Which means mc is already running memoro's `sqlite` and `heavy` files at seven-way parallelism without knowing which ones they are — memoro's selector does not report the resource class. `printablePlan` in `scripts/testing/ci.mjs` emits `files`, `selectedBindings`, `impacts` and `commands`, and not `classifications`, even though `buildExecutionBatches` in `runner.mjs:17` has them.

So the ordering step cannot simply raise a number: it needs to know which files may not run beside others. That is a memoro change, and step 6 names it as a pull request in the memoro worktree of this workarea.

what_the_code_taught_us.title: Ruling 4 is the design, and it is half built
body: `docs/project/mc/rulings.md` § 4, ruled 2026-08-29, raised as `mc-test-1`, owner `mc-test`. It says of itself: *"No `mc-test` plan exists. This ruling is not carried by any plan."* This plan is that carrier.

Built: the verb (`src/mc/commands/test.js`), one shared `runGate` for both doors, condition 1 — memoro's `scripts/testing/runner.mjs` no longer stops after a red batch and `tapTotals` in `src/mc/tap-red.js` sums every process's summary, and part of condition 2, the verdict's reach.

Not built: measurement A as ruled — the candidate side alone, compared against main's recorded red set — because what shipped instead was `select`, which runs the same file list on **both** sides. Not built: B, the full run that writes that set, so `.mc/red-ratchet.json` is still a hand-maintained floor and condition 3, the report carrying B's age, cannot be satisfied at all.

documents.label: Why what a repository needs is declared and never guessed

steps.title: Run the command gates the selection already reported
steps.done_when: A round over a pull request touching only `public/css/` reports `css:lint` and `css:tokens` in its verdict, each with a timing and a pass/fail, and a pull request that breaks `i18n:contract` comes back red naming that command.
instruction: `selectFiles` in `src/mc/repo-gate.js` parses the selector's JSON and keeps `parsed?.files`. The same JSON carries `commands` — an array of `{ id, packageScript, passBaseRef, resourceClass, selectedBy }` — and nothing reads it. Keep them, alongside the files, on the object `selectFiles` returns.

Run them on the **candidate only**, after the suite, in the order the selector gave. They are gates about the change, not measurements of two trees: `css:tokens` and `i18n:contract` take `--base-ref` and are already differential in themselves, and running them on the baseline would measure main against main. Pass `--base-ref <baseRef>` when `passBaseRef` is true, exactly as memoro's own `scripts/testing/ci.mjs` does in `runPackageCommand` — `npm run <packageScript> -- --base-ref <ref>`. Use the same `resourceClass` field to decide exclusivity if a lease is taken; `standard` needs none.

Run every command even after one fails, and report all of their results. `ci.mjs` made this choice explicitly and wrote down why: while any selected test is red, a skipped command gate hides every contract regression it would have caught. Copy the behaviour, not the code.

Report each command in the verdict the way `report.extra_gates` is already reported — name, command, duration, ok — and make the round's `ok` depend on them. A command that fails is the change's doing in the same sense a new red test is: these gates are diff-scoped by construction.

This overlaps `extra_gates` and should not duplicate it. `extra_gates` is what an operator declares beside the suite; this is what the repository's own selector chose for this diff. Keep both, report them in one list with a field saying which is which, and leave `extra_gates` empty for memoro as it is now.

Verify against a real pull request, not a fixture: pick an open memoro PR that touches `public/css/`, run `mc test memoro <pr>`, and read the verdict. Then contrive the negative — a branch with an `i18n` violation — and confirm the round is red for that reason and says so.

steps.title: The instruction the repository owns
steps.done_when: `declarationFor` reads `.mc/test.json` from the repository under test, layered shipped < repository file < `~/mc/repo-gates.json`; a repository with no such file behaves exactly as it does today; and `affected` is present in `normalise()` so `repo-freshen`'s declared path is live.
instruction: `src/mc/repo-gate-table.js` holds, in mc's own source, memoro's `prepare`, `prepare_why`, `select`, `select_why`, `pr_tests_flags` and `merge_log` — and memoro-cli's. Every change to how a repository tests itself is therefore a memoro-cli release. The file's own header explains at length why what a repository needs must be *written down* rather than guessed; this step keeps that rule and moves the writing to where the repository can do it.

Add a third layer to `declarationFor`: `SHIPPED` first, then `<repoPath>/.mc/test.json` if it parses, then `readOverrides(root)` — the operator's file stays the last word, because it is how a machine-local fact gets in without a release. A file that will not parse is a stop with a reason, never a silent fall-through to the shipped entry; the whole point of this table is that a partial declaration stops as hard as a missing one.

Report the layer each field came from in the declaration result, the way `shadowed` already names the fields an override silently dropped. Whoever reads a refusal needs to know which of three files to edit.

Add `affected: entry.affected ?? null` to `normalise()`. It is missing on main, so `repo-freshen.js` — whose header says it runs the repository's declared `affected` — never runs anything. This is one line and it is the field ruling 4's measurement A is built on.
Do not ship a `.mc/test.json` in memoro from this step. The reader lands first and changes nothing on its own; memoro's file is step 3, and it is a pull request in the other repository.

Cover all three precedence levels in `tests/mc/repo-gate-table.test.js`, including the unparseable file, the partially-specified repository file, and a repository with no file at all — that last one asserting the declaration is byte-identical to today's.

steps.title: memoro's own instruction, in memoro
steps.done_when: `memoro/.mc/test.json` carries memoro's `prepare`, `select`, `affected` and `pr_tests_flags` with the evidence for each, `mc test memoro <pr>` reads them from there rather than from mc's shipped table, and removing the file leaves the round unchanged.
instruction: **This step's pull request is in the memoro worktree of this workarea, not in memoro-cli.** Branch it from `origin/main` in `~/mc/mc-test/memoro`. It is a small file plus a paragraph of documentation, and it is the first proof that step 2's reader works against a real repository.

Copy memoro's entry out of `SHIPPED` verbatim — `prepare: "npm ci"` with its D-0089 evidence, `select`, `select_why`, `pr_tests_flags: ["--import", "./tests/_helpers/browser-paths.mjs"]` — and add `affected: "npm run ci -- --base-ref origin/main"`, which ruling 4 declared and nothing has carried. Keep the `prepare_why` and `select_why` prose: `repo-gate-table.js`'s header makes the rule that a `_why` may never carry a provenance that does not exist, and copying the existing text preserves real provenance rather than inventing new.

Leave `merge_log` out of the repository's file. Where a merge is written down is mc's business and the operator's, not the repository's, and it resolves against the work root — a path that has no meaning inside a checkout.

Say in `AGENTS.md` § *Tests* that this file exists and what reads it, in two or three sentences, so a session changing how memoro tests knows where the declaration lives. Do not restate the contents; point at the file.

Leave mc's shipped memoro entry in place. It is the fallback for a checkout that predates the file, and step 2's precedence test asserts the file wins. Deleting it is a separate decision about how long mc supports old checkouts, and this project does not take it.

steps.title: Measurement A: the candidate alone, against a recorded set
steps.done_when: A round runs no baseline suite; its JSON report names the commit the comparison set was measured at and how many commits ago, warns loudly when that is stale, and never refuses on staleness alone.
instruction: This is ruling 4's measurement A, and it is the single largest speed change in this plan: the round stops running the same work twice. Read § 4 of `docs/project/mc/rulings.md` before starting — the shape, the three non-negotiable conditions, and the reasoning are all there, and this instruction does not repeat them.

Today `runGate` runs `measureSelected` on the baseline worktree and again on the candidate, and `compareRed` calls the difference. A replaces the baseline run with a set read from disk: the repository's known red names at a named commit. The comparison rule is unchanged — a name red on the candidate and absent from the recorded set is this change's doing — and `compareRed` should not need to change at all.

Where the set lives and what writes it is step 5. Until it does, A must degrade honestly rather than pretend: with no recorded set, or one whose commit is not an ancestor of the base, the round says so and runs the baseline as it does today. A missing set is not an empty set — reading it as empty would call every standing red name a new regression.

Condition 1 of the ruling is satisfied and should be verified, not assumed: `memoro/scripts/testing/runner.mjs` no longer breaks after a red batch, and `tapTotals` in `src/mc/tap-red.js` sums every `# tests` line rather than keeping the last. Confirm both still hold before A goes live — if either regresses, A and the recorded set are two truncated measurements that match each other and read as "no new red".

Condition 3 is this step's own: the report carries the set's age. Ruling 4 also settled that staleness **warns loudly and does not refuse** — *"En grind som vägrar på en tidsstämpel blir en grind folk går runt"*. Put the age in the verdict text a person reads, not only in the JSON.

`.mc/red-ratchet.json` is a different thing and must not be conflated with the recorded set. Read the header of `src/mc/red-ratchet.js` first: it is an agreed floor for main, it is reported and never refuses, and its one stop — a diff that removes names while those tests are still red — is about the change's own claim. A is a comparison set; the ratchet is a statement about main. They may share a file format; they do not share a meaning.

steps.title: Measurement B: the full run that writes what A compares against
steps.done_when: A B run over a repository writes its red set with the commit it was measured at, `mc test <repo> --full` triggers one by hand, and the runner starts one when it is otherwise idle.
instruction: B is the other half of ruling 4: the whole suite on one tree, recording the red set A subtracts. The coupling is the point — B produces exactly what A compares against — so the file B writes and the file A reads are one format defined once.

Record per repository: the commit, the timestamp, the red test names, and the totals the run printed including how many processes reported them (`tapTotals` returns `runs` for exactly this reason). A truncated B is worse than none, so a B whose `runs` count is lower than the number of batches the suite should have produced is recorded as unusable rather than as a clean set.

Trigger it two ways. By hand, `mc test <repo> --full`, so a person can refresh the set after a merge storm. And from the runner when it is idle — ruling 4 points at `run.js:279`, the 600-second sleep, as the place. Check that line still exists and still means idle before wiring into it; the runner has been rewritten since the ruling was written.

B is slow by definition and must never block a merge or a step session. It takes the repository's suite lease (`src/mc/suite-lease.js`) at background priority, and it yields: a `mc test` or `mc merge` round that arrives while B is running wins, and B restarts or abandons rather than making the round wait. A round that waits ten minutes for a background measurement is the thing this whole project exists to prevent.

Write down, in `docs/technical/mc-merge.md` or a sibling, what the two measurements are and which one a reader is looking at. The names A and B are this plan's; the document should use words a person recognises.

steps.title: memoro's selection says what class each file is, and its cap reads the machine
steps.done_when: `node scripts/testing/ci.mjs --list --json` prints a resource class for every selected file, and `npm run ci` over an identical diff is faster on this machine as a median of three runs before and after.
instruction: **This step's pull request is in the memoro worktree of this workarea.** It exists because the ordering step cannot run without it: mc currently spawns `node --test` over memoro's selected files with no `--test-concurrency` at all, which means Node's default of seven, which means memoro's `sqlite` and `heavy` files are already running seven-wide in every round without mc knowing which they are.

`printablePlan` in `scripts/testing/ci.mjs` emits `files`, `selectedBindings`, `impacts` and `commands`. Add the resource class per file. `buildExecutionBatches` in `scripts/testing/runner.mjs:17` already builds a `Map` of `plan.classifications`, so the data exists and the change is to report it, not to compute it. Keep `files` exactly as it is — an existing consumer reads it.

`RESOURCE_CAPACITY = 2` in `scripts/testing/resource-coordinator.mjs:15` is a constant on an eight-core machine, and `RESOURCE_BATCHES` in `runner.mjs:10` declares `standard: 2`. Make the capacity read `os.availableParallelism()` with a floor of the present value, so no machine gets slower, and leave `sqlite` and `heavy` at one — their exclusivity is a correctness property, not a tuning knob.

Measure this one properly, because the numbers are noisy: the twenty `tests/surface-runtime` files in this plan's lessons ran 11.1, 12.4 and 9.3 s at concurrency 2, and 8.1 s at four. That is a 30 % spread between identical runs, so report a median of at least three, on an otherwise idle machine, and say what the machine was doing.

Do not touch which files are selected, which profile they belong to, or the registry's membership. This step changes what the plan *reports* and how many lanes the runner may use, and nothing about what is run.

steps.title: Know what each file costs, and start the expensive ones first
steps.done_when: A cost table under `~/mc/` carries per-file wall times per repository after two rounds; the file list a round runs is ordered descending by recorded cost within each resource class; and the twenty-file `surface-runtime` list runs in a median of at most 6.0 s over five runs.
instruction: The measurement that motivates this step: of twenty `tests/surface-runtime` files, four carry about 17.5 s of roughly 23 s serial — 6.19, 4.05, 3.87 and 3.41 s against a tail of about 0.3 s each. The heaviest file alone is 4.33 s warm, which is the floor. Alphabetical order over eight lanes gives 8–11 s; longest-first should approach the floor. Nothing here is speculative except the last sentence, which is what this step tests.

Record per-file wall time as the round runs. `measureSelected` currently spawns one `node --test` over the whole list, which gives no per-file times — the TAP output does, in each file's own duration. Parse them from the TAP the round already captures rather than spawning per file; a process per file would cost more than it saves, and `node -e ""` alone is 0.05 s while a `surface-runtime` file is 4 s, so the overhead is not where the time goes.

Store the table under `~/mc/`, keyed by repository and path, with the timestamp of the reading. Treat it as a hint and never as truth: an unknown file sorts as if it were expensive, because starting a long file late is the failure this step exists to avoid, and starting a short one early costs nothing.

Order within a resource class, never across one. `sqlite` and `heavy` are exclusive for correctness — step 6 makes the class visible in the selection, and this step must respect it. A repository whose selector does not report classes gets one class and one lane budget, which is what it has today.
Assert the ordering in a unit test against a synthetic cost table, not against a timing. A test that asserts wall time is a test that fails on a busy laptop.

Then measure the criterion: the same twenty files, five runs, median at most 6.0 s, machine otherwise idle. If longest-first does not reach it, report the number reached and what bounded it — the 4.33 s floor may simply be most of the answer, and that is a finding, not a failure. Do not chase the number by changing what runs.

steps.title: Say what the round cost and how far it reached
steps.done_when: A round's report names its phases with timings, the ten most expensive files it ran, the commands it ran beside them, and the reach sentence — how many files the selection chose and what it is blind to — and `docs/technical/mc-merge.md` describes the round as it now is.
instruction: The round already times phases and already carries a reach sentence for a selected round. This step finishes condition 2 of ruling 4 and makes the cost visible to whoever is waiting for it.

Report, in the human verdict and not only the JSON: the phases with their timings; the ten most expensive files of this round from the cost table; each command gate with its own duration; and the age of the comparison set from step 4. A person reading a slow round should be able to see which four files it was without asking.

Keep the existing honesty about reach. The verdict must keep saying when the selector gave up and ran everything, and it must keep naming what the selection cannot see — memoro's selection follows pins now, but a reach sentence that stops being true is worse than none. Check what the current blindness number is before restating it; do not copy 2,114 forward without re-running `memoro/scripts/testing/blindness.mjs`.

Rewrite the round's description in `docs/technical/mc-merge.md` to match what the round now does: one measured side, a recorded comparison set with an age, the repository's own instruction, the command gates, the ordering. Delete the description of the two-sided file-list round rather than leaving it beside the new one — this repository has been bitten before by two places answering one question about one repository, and `repo-gate-table.js`'s header says so in as many words.
Add a line to `docs/project/mc/rulings.md` § 4 recording that a plan now carries it, replacing the sentence that says none does.
